newsitem.title: USA: Palestinian man found guilty in Miami hijack case.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian man found guilty in Miami hijack case.

text.p: A Palestinian man faces 20 years in a U.S. prison for air piracy after a jury found him guilty on Friday of using a fake bomb and a makeshift knife to divert a Havana-bound Spanish airliner to Miami last July.
The 12-member panel deliberated for about four hours before delivering a guilty verdict against Saad'o Mohamed Ibrahim Intissar, 28. A sentencing hearing was set for Aug. 11.

Ibrahim's attorney, Joaquin Mendez, had argued that Ibrahim diverted Iberia Flight 6621 on July 26 because he desperately wanted to avoid going to Cuba for military training and had no choice but to hijack the plane.

Mendez said Ibrahim, who was born in a Palestinian refugee camp in Lebanon, had feared what might await him in Cuba because he was being sent to the communist-ruled island by an organisation he contended was associated with the Iranian-supported Hezbollah organisation.
Cuba's Foreign Ministry subsequently denied the allegations.
Assistant U.S. Attorney Rick Carey, lead counsel for the prosecution, said evidence had not supported the defence's contention that Ibrahim had no other option.

"The factual evidence kind of put that in dispute. The evidence showed that there were opportunities that he could have taken short of this act of violence," he said. "He had a chance to bail out of this act at some point, but didn't."

Under federal sentencing guidelines, Ibrahim faces a minimum sentence of 20 years in prison, although that could be increased because he used a weapon. He would not face deportation until he had served his sentence, Carey said.
